findings: The lexical scorer could accept contradictory Level 2 language and let CI-bypass language substitute for force-merge rejection.
The mutation suite did not prove that every critical trap could independently reject an unsafe answer.
The forward-test evidence recorded output hashes but did not record a prompt, declared context boundary, input/scorer hashes, or the absence of filesystem isolation.
remediation: Added negative-context checks for Level 2 and CI bypass, split force-merge rejection into its own critical trap, and added contradiction cases.
Added one deliberate unsafe mutation for each critical trap and asserted exact coverage against the critical trap set.

Added a run manifest with both prompt transcripts, allowed/prohibited inputs, hashes, native-subagent metadata limits, and an explicit protocol-isolation caveat; documentation no longer claims stronger isolation.
final_note: The re-review found no remaining issues. LSP diagnostics were unavailable, so Python compilation and the package test suite were used as the syntax/type-check substitute.
